'''Hans Victor Westerhoff''' (born 14 January 1953)<ref name=album>[http://albumacademicum.uva.nl/id/id001863 Prof. dr. H.V. Westerhoff, 1953-] at the [[University of Amsterdam]] ''Album Academicum'' website</ref> is a Dutch biologist and biochemist who is professor of synthetic [[systems biology]] at the [[University of Amsterdam]]<ref>{{cite web|publisher=University of Amsterdam|url=http://www.uva.nl/en/about-the-uva/organisation/staff-members/content/w/e/h.v.westerhoff/h.v.westerhoff.html|title=Prof. Dr. H.V. (Hans) Westerhoff|access-date=9 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131212041237/http://www.uva.nl/en/about-the-uva/organisation/staff-members/content/w/e/h.v.westerhoff/h.v.westerhoff.html|archive-date=12 December 2013}}</ref> and [[AstraZeneca]] professor of systems biology at the [[University of Manchester]].<ref name=googlescholar>{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=YOCnveEAAAAJ&hl=en|title=Hans Westerhoff|publisher=[[Google Scholar]]|access-date=9 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131218103918/http://scholar.google.com/citations?user=YOCnveEAAAAJ&hl=en|archive-date=18 December 2013}}</ref> Currently he is a Chair of AstraZeneca and a director of the [[Manchester Centre for Integrative Systems Biology]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Professor Hans Westerhoff|publisher=University of Manchester|access-date=9 December 2013|url=http://www.shapeofscience.manchester.ac.uk/speakers/hanswesterhoff/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131215071331/http://www.shapeofscience.manchester.ac.uk/speakers/hanswesterhoff/|archive-date=15 December 2013}}</ref><ref name=scopus>{{Scopus|id=7101854663}}</ref>

==Career==
Westerhoff was born in [[Amsterdam]], Netherlands. He was educated at the [[University of Amsterdam]] where he was awarded a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in 1983 for investigations of [[non-equilibrium thermodynamics]] and the control of [[biological thermodynamics]] supervised by Karel van Dam.<ref name=album/> In 1996 he succeeded [[Ad Stouthamer]] as professor of microbiology at the [[Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam]].<ref>{{cite web|author=Martine Zuidweg |url=https://www.trouw.nl/nieuws/de-confrontatie~bd1ad356/ |title=De confrontatie |language=nl |publisher=Trouw |date=11 June 1997 |access-date=19 July 2020}}</ref>

==Research==
At the beginning of his career Westerhoff worked in the area of [[non-equilibrium thermodynamics]] in relation to [[Transduction (biophysics)|biological energy transduction]].<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1016/0005-2728(80)90179-6|journal = Biochim. Biophys. Acta | title = Linear relation between rate and thermodynamic force in enzyme-catalyzed reactions | last1 = Van der Meer | first1 = R | last2 =Westerhoff | first2 = H V | last3 = Van Dam  | first3 = K |volume = 591|number=2|pages = 488–493|year=1980|pmid = 7397133 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1073/pnas.78.6.3554|journal = Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA | volume = 78|number = 1|pages = 3554–3558 | year = 1981 | title = Mosaic non-equilibrium thermodynamics describes biological energy transduction| last1 =Westerhoff | first1 = H V | last5 = Van Dam  | first5 = K | last2 = Hellingwerf | first2 = K J  | last3 = Arents  | first3 = J C | last4 = Scholte | first4 = B J|pmid = 6267598 |pmc = 319608 |bibcode = 1981PNAS...78.3554W |doi-access = free }}</ref> His work on this topic led to a book written with Karel Van Dam.<ref>{{cite book| isbn= 978-0-444-80783-0  | title = Thermodynamics and Control of Biological Free-Energy Transduction | last1 =Westerhoff | first1 = H V | last2 = Van Dam  | first2 = K|publisher = Elsevier | year = 1987}}</ref>

After being a coauthor of one of the first experimental papers to stimulate interest in [[metabolic control analysis]]<ref>{{cite journal| last1 = Groen| first1 = AK| last2 = Wanders| first2 = RJA| last3 = Westerhoff| first3 = HV| last4 = van de Meer| first4 = R| last5 = Tager| first5 = JM| title = Quantification of the contribution of various steps to the control of mitochondrial respiration| journal = Journal of Biological Chemistry | year = 1982| volume = 257| issue = 6| pages = 2754–2757| doi = 10.1016/S0021-9258(19)81026-8| pmid = 7061448| doi-access = free}}</ref> and participating in the group that proposed a harmonized terminology,<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Burns | first1 = J.A. | last2 = Cornish-Bowden | first2 = A. | last3 = Groen | first3 = A.K. | last4 = Heinrich | first4 = R. | last5 = Kacser | first5 = H. | last6 = Porteous | first6 = J.W. | last7 = Rapoport | first7 = S.M. | last8 = Rapoport | first8 = T.A. | last9 = Stucki | first9 = J.W. | last10 = Tager | first10 = J.M. | last11 = Wanders | first11 = R.J.A. | last12 = Westerhoff | first12 = H.V. | year = 1985 | title = Control analysis of metabolic systems | journal = Trends Biochem. Sci. | volume = 10 | page = 16 | doi=10.1016/0968-0004(85)90008-8}}</ref> Westerhoff moved progressively towards working on multi-enzyme systems as his major activity, starting with an analysis of the effect of enzyme activity on metabolite concentrations.<ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1111/j.1432-1033.1984.tb08304.x | journal = Eur. J. Biochem.  | year = 1984 | volume = 142 | number = 2 | pages = 425–430 | title = How do enzyme activities control metabolite concentrations? An additional theorem in the theory of metabolic control| last1 = Westerhoff | first1 = Hans V. | last2 = Chen | first2 = Yi-Der | pmid = 6745283 | doi-access = free }}</ref> He published many papers in this area, of which one may note an analysis of the control of regulatory cascades,<ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1016/S0022-5193(05)80426-6 | journal = J. Theor. Biol. | last2 = Westerhoff | first2 = H.V. | last1 = Kahn | first1 = D | volume = 153 | number= 2  | pages = 255–285 | title = Control theory of regulatory cascades| year = 1991 | pmid = 1686290 | bibcode = 1991JThBi.153..255K }}</ref> analysqis of glycolytic oscilations in yeast,<ref>{{Cite journal| pmid = 10692299| pmc = 1300712| year = 2000| last1 = Bier| first1 = M| title = How yeast cells synchronize their glycolytic oscillations: A perturbation analytic treatment| journal = Biophys. J.| volume = 78| issue = 3| pages = 1087–93| last2 = Bakker| first2 = B. M.| last3 = Westerhoff| first3 = H. V.| doi = 10.1016/S0006-3495(00)76667-7| bibcode = 2000BpJ....78.1087B
}}</ref> and showing that the ''in vivo'' behaviour of ''Trypanosoma brucei''  agreed with the kinetic properties of the glycolytic enzymes.<ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1074/jbc.272.6.3207 | journal = J. Biol. Chem.  |  title = Glycolysis in bloodstream form ''Trypanosoma brucei'' can be understood in terms of the kinetics of the glycolytic enzymes | last1 = Bakker | first1 = B M | last2 =  Michels | first2 = P A M | last3 = Opperdoes | first3 = F R  | last4 =Westerhoff  | first4= H V | year=1997 | volume = 272 | number = 6  | pages = 3207–3215| pmid = 9013556 | doi-access = free }}</ref>

Westerhoff and colleagues discovered [[magainin]] in the [[African clawed frog]] which helps it fight against [[bacteria]].<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1111/j.1432-1033.1995.0257n.x| pmid = 7705337| title = Functional Synergism of the Magainins PGLa and Magainin-2 in Escherichia coli, Tumor Cells and Liposomes| journal = European Journal of Biochemistry| volume = 228| issue = 2| pages = 257–64| year = 1995| last1 = Westerhoff | first1 = H. | url = https://pure.uva.nl/ws/files/2903967/959_11104y.pdf}}</ref> In December 1996 he and his group discovered a [[nitric-oxide reductase]] of ''[[Paracoccus denitrificans]]''.<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1111/j.1432-1033.1996.0592r.x| pmid = 9022686| title = Mutational Analysis of the nor Gene Cluster which Encodes Nitric-Oxide Reductase from Paracoccus denitrificans| journal = European Journal of Biochemistry| volume = 242| issue = 3| pages = 592–600| year = 1996| last1 = Boer | first1 = A. M. | doi-access = free }}</ref> <!--In 2000 he and Martin Bier, along with Barbara Bakker discovered that [[yeast]] cells can [[glycolytic oscillation|oscillate]] and merge with others in some cases because they get energized from [[glycolysis]].</ref>-->
